title: Products of integral morphisms are integral
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $J$ be a small set, and let $g_j:T_j\to S$ be integral morphisms [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] for $j\in J$. For the product $T=\prod_{j\in J}T_j$ supplied by [lem-trf-affine-infinite-product-existence], the projection $T\to S$ is integral.

proof.text: Write $q:T\to S$ for the structure map. By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], every $g_j$ is affine. Apply [lem-trf-affine-infinite-product-existence]. Its affine projection to the finite product indexed by the empty subset is precisely $q$, since that finite product is $S$. Thus $q$ is affine. For an arbitrary affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$, put $X=q^{-1}(U)$ and $X_j=g_j^{-1}(U)$. By [pqf-def-affine-morphism] these are affine, say $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $X_j=\operatorname{Spec}B_j$. The maps $A\to B_j$ are integral by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0CNK, lemma-infinite-product-integral, affine-piece hint, expanded using Tag 0CNI (lemma-infinite-product)

proof.text: The restricted projections exhibit $X$ as the product of the $X_j$ over $U$. Indeed, for any scheme $V\to U$, a family of $U$-maps $V\to X_j$ gives $S$-maps $V\to T_j$ and hence a unique $S$-map $h:V\to T$. Its composite to $S$ is the given map through $U$, so its image is contained in $q^{-1}(U)=X$. It factors uniquely through this open subscheme: restrict the codomain of its continuous map to $X$ and the sheaf map to opens of $X$; the local maps on stalks are the same. The same restriction identifies maps to $X_j$ with maps to $T_j$ over the given $V\to U$. Uniqueness in the product $T$ gives uniqueness in $X$. This is just the definition of an open subscheme/open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and the product universal property.

source.place: Tag 0CNK, lemma-infinite-product-integral, affine-piece hint, expanded using Tag 0CNI (lemma-infinite-product)

proof.text: Let $\iota_j:B_j\to B$ be the $A$-algebra homomorphisms corresponding to the restricted projections. The ring $B$ is a coproduct of the $B_j$ in commutative $A$-algebras: for any commutative $A$-algebra $D$, the correspondence between ring homomorphisms and morphisms of spectra in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies $A$-maps $B\to D$ with $U$-maps $\operatorname{Spec}D\to X$, and $A$-maps $B_j\to D$ with $U$-maps $\operatorname{Spec}D\to X_j$. Step 2 gives the required bijection between the former maps and families of the latter maps. Functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ identifies its restriction maps with precomposition by the $\iota_j$.

source.place: Tag 0CNK, lemma-infinite-product-integral, affine-piece hint, expanded using Tag 0CNI (lemma-infinite-product)

proof.text: Every element in every image $\iota_j(B_j)$ is integral over $A$. Namely, if $b\in B_j$ satisfies $b^n+\sum_{k<n}a_kb^k=0$, using the structure map $A\to B_j$ for its coefficients, then applying the $A$-algebra map $\iota_j$ gives $\iota_j(b)^n+\sum_{k<n}a_k\iota_j(b)^k=0$ in $B$. This is a monic equation over $A$, so proves the assertion directly from the definition of integral elements in [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].

source.place: Tag 0CNK, lemma-infinite-product-integral, affine-piece hint, expanded using Tag 0CNI (lemma-infinite-product)

proof.text: Let $C\subseteq B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $B$. The statement of [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] says exactly that $C$ is a subring containing the image of $A$, with underlying set all elements integral over $A$; hence it is an $A$-algebra. Step 4 shows that each $\iota_j$ factors as an $A$-algebra map $\bar\iota_j:B_j\to C$ followed by the inclusion $e:C\hookrightarrow B$. Apply the coproduct universal property of Step 3 with $D=C$ to obtain $r:B\to C$ satisfying $r\iota_j=\bar\iota_j$ for every $j$.

source.place: Tags 00GO (lemma-integral-closure-is-ring), 00GP (definition-integral-closure); applied to the affine-piece hint of Limits Tag 0CNK

proof.text: The $A$-algebra maps $er$ and $\operatorname{id}_B$ have the same composites with every $\iota_j$, because $er\iota_j=e\bar\iota_j=\iota_j$. Uniqueness in Step 3 gives $er=\operatorname{id}_B$. Consequently every $b\in B$ equals $e(r(b))$, so belongs to $C$ and is integral over $A$. This holds for every affine open $U\subseteq S$. Together with the affineness of $q$ from Step 1, [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] now gives that $q$ is integral. The argument includes $J=\varnothing$: the coproduct universal property is then the initial $A$-algebra property, and the same uniqueness calculation holds without any factor maps.
